admin.agent.title: Agent API
admin.agent.description: Let agents operate this admin panel through Skills or MCP.
admin.agent.quickstart_hint: Issue a key for an agent in the Agents tab, then connect one of these ways.
admin.agent.logs_hint: Every call an agent made with its key: who, which key, what, on which record, and the outcome. Calls rejected for missing permission or invalid input aren't run, so they aren't listed.
admin.agent.mcp_json: Other MCP clients (Cursor, Codex, Claude Desktop…), mcp.json:
admin.agent.skill_hint: Copy this prompt to your agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw…), then send it the key you issued under Agents. The agent saves each project's URL and key in a private local credentials file (readable only by you), never in a repository. For several projects, copy the prompt from this page on each site. Note: the key stays in the chat history — revoke it under Agents if it leaks or is no longer needed.
admin.agent.skill_prompt:
Please add "{app}" ({url}) as a project you can manage, under the project name "{name}".

1. If you don't have the site-admin skill yet, download these two files into a site-admin folder in your skills directory (e.g. ~/.claude/skills/site-admin/). If it's already installed, skip this step and don't overwrite it: the client can read every project's key, so update it only when I explicitly ask, from a site I trust.
   - {url}/api/admin/agent/skill?file=SKILL.md → site-admin/SKILL.md
   - {url}/api/admin/agent/skill?file=admin-client.mjs → site-admin/scripts/admin-client.mjs
2. I'll send you this project's admin key (starts with sa_admin_) next. Save it via stdin — never as a command argument — and never repeat it afterwards:
   printf '%s' '<key>' | node <skill-dir>/scripts/admin-client.mjs add {name} {url}
3. Run node <skill-dir>/scripts/admin-client.mjs --project {name} list and tell me which operations you can call.
4. From then on, follow SKILL.md strictly for the admin tasks I give you; when managing several projects, name the project with --project on every call.
admin.agent.full_docs: Full reference (idempotency, audit, local stdio MCP bridge, CLI agent/key management): docs/admin-agent.md in the repository.
admin.agent.never_warning: A non-expiring key works until you revoke it. Give the agent minimal roles, and revoke the key as soon as it's no longer needed or may have leaked.
admin.agent.created_warning: Copy this key now — it won't be shown again. Store it in the agent's secret store, never in the repository.
admin.agent.revoke_warning: Revoke this key? Agents using it lose access immediately. This can't be undone.
admin.agent.accounts_hint: Each agent is an API-type user: its permissions are the RBAC roles you assign, and it signs in only with its admin API keys. Agents aren't counted as users.
admin.agent.agent_form_hint: Pick the roles this agent acts with. You can only grant roles whose permissions you hold yourself.
admin.agent.no_agents: No agents yet. Create one, assign roles, then issue a key.
admin.agent.keys_hint: Admin API keys (sa_admin_…) for this agent. Only a hash is stored; a key is shown once. They never work on the product API.
admin.agent.delete_warning: The agent account, its role assignments and all its keys are removed. Agents using them lose access immediately. Its execution history is kept.

admin.operations.description: Follow the first visit through to payment. Compare the same hours, find the drop-off, and keep a record of every experiment.

admin.operations.cohort_hint: Cohort: first visit in the selected period, followed through to now. One browser ID per visitor; linked users count only in their earliest browser cohort. Steps count distinct cohort members, not impressions; plan selection is optional. AI users have created a task. Source, country, entry page and build never change on return visits. Staff, service accounts and test browsers are excluded. Top 100 groups shown.
admin.operations.daily_hint: Calendar days in UTC+08:00. Sign-ups are counted by registration date; payers and orders by payment date. Today is partial.
admin.operations.method_source: Adapted from the supplied Gefei operations notes: keep data in your database, compare matching hours, investigate the funnel and record each experiment. Case-study claims and screenshots are reference material, not this site’s results.
admin.operations.method_metrics: Revenue is grouped by the actual payment currency, in its correct minor units. It includes renewals in the daily totals and subtracts recorded refunds from the original paid orders; refunds therefore revise the original payment day. Cohort revenue excludes renewals. Completed tasks determine AI success rate; pending tasks are shown separately. A dash means no observations or no denominator.
admin.operations.method_experiments: The journal stores observations, hypotheses, changes, build versions and reviews. Sample targets are plans, not measured traffic. It does not allocate A/B traffic or estimate a winning probability. Define the product variants, exposure event and attribution window before enabling a live experiment.
admin.operations.method_tracking: Visitor collection starts after this feature is installed, honors cookie consent, Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control, and ignores known bots and private pages. Local development usually has no country header. Open a fresh test browser with ?ops_test=1 on its first visit to exclude that browser. Build IDs come from Git at build time; deployments may override VITE_BUILD_ID. Anonymous traffic is browser-based and cannot identify the same person across devices.
admin.operations.experiments_hint: Record the data, hypothesis and change before experimenting; save the evidence and outcome afterward. This journal does not change live traffic or pricing.

video.gallery.title: Watch what MAGI-2 can make
video.gallery.references.home: MAGI-2 examples here include an animated familiar and a wide shot of a desert mech fight. Compare them with the filmed coastal reference to see how the horizon and camera angle change the sense of scale.
video.gallery.references.text: Study a few seconds of atmosphere, motion, and camera direction before you describe your shot.
video.gallery.references.image: See how light, texture, and motion can bring a product photo to life.
video.gallery.higgsfield.title: MAGI-2 showcase
video.gallery.higgsfield.description: MAGI-2 showcase clips from Higgsfield put three techniques side by side. Watch the camera reposition, cut on action, and use light trails to carry movement across the frame.
video.reference.coast.title: Last light on the coast
video.reference.coast.description: Look for the line that leads your eye from the foreground to the horizon. Describe where the coast sits in the frame before specifying the camera move.
video.reference.cup.title: A quiet coffee break
video.reference.cup.description: Notice how the light and framing set the mood before anything moves. Give your opening shot one subject and one clear source of light.
video.reference.waves.title: Waves rolling ashore
video.reference.waves.description: Describe which direction the water moves and how it breaks. A visible action gives a short shot a clear beginning and ending.
video.reference.forest.title: An autumn forest walk
video.reference.forest.description: Follow the path as warm light filters through the trees. Use the path as a visual anchor when describing forward camera movement.
video.reference.dropper.title: Skincare in close-up
video.reference.dropper.description: The dropper and glass edges catch the light. Specify where the highlight falls and which product details should stay sharp.
video.reference.spray.title: A burst of perfume mist
video.reference.spray.description: Watch the mist lift away from the bottle. Use a single burst or another clearly timed action to introduce movement around a product.
video.reference.serum.title: Serum in motion
video.reference.serum.description: The drops give the close-up a clear point of focus. Describe the surface, the size of the drop, and what changes on impact.
video.gallery.unpublished: The release page does not publish the full prompt or all render settings for this clip.

video.example.styles.description: A continuous move carries the scene from one painterly treatment into the next. Watch the transitions at the edges of the frame.
video.example.styles.input: Five classic paintings guide the style changes in a 30-second take.
video.example.flowers.title: Giant Flower World
video.example.flowers.description: Observe which parts of the wardrobe and character design persist as the camera moves between flower-filled locations.
video.example.flowers.input: Character, wardrobe, and floral-scene references are shown in the original release.
video.example.cuts.title: Directing the Cut
video.example.cuts.description: The showcase demonstrates timed cuts between shots. Look for how the action carries through each change in framing.
video.example.cuts.input: Sand.ai describes timed shot changes in the showcase.
video.example.editing.title: Editing a Take
video.example.editing.description: An example of targeted video editing. Compare the subject and background across the transition.
video.example.editing.input: The original report demonstrates an edit to an existing video.
video.example.lunar.title: Lunar Cave
video.example.lunar.description: A cave scene used in Sand.ai’s post-training comparison. Inspect rock texture and edge detail as the camera moves.
video.example.lunar.input: The release provides a side-by-side 1080p, 25 fps comparison around 25 seconds long.
video.example.alpine.title: Alpine Lake
video.example.alpine.description: A landscape from Sand.ai’s post-training comparison. Follow the shoreline and check how details hold steady as the view changes.
video.example.alpine.input: Sand.ai published an earlier and a later version of the same alpine lake scene.
video.example.storm-wings.title: Storm Wings
video.example.storm-wings.summary: The camera shifts around a winged fighter as cool blue gives way to amber.
video.example.storm-wings.description: Follow a winged fighter through contrasting blue and amber light as the camera changes position. Watch how the rim light keeps the wings readable as the fighter turns.
video.example.ember-vortex.title: Ember Vortex
video.example.ember-vortex.summary: A wide view of the red vortex cuts in close to show the fighter’s reaction.
video.example.ember-vortex.description: A fight inside a red vortex cuts between full-body movement and tight reactions. Notice how the wide shot establishes where the fighter stands before the close shots pick out individual movements.
video.example.solar-guardian.title: Solar Guardian
video.example.solar-guardian.summary: Purple and gold light trails draw the eye across the frame as the armored figure moves.
video.example.solar-guardian.description: A gold-armored figure moves through purple and gold frames with graphic light trails. Watch the direction of those trails to see how the effects reinforce the movement of the figure.
video.example.cosmic-familiar.title: Cosmic Familiar
video.example.cosmic-familiar.descriptio: A small winged creature moves from a starry backdrop to a rocky landscape. Watch how its face and glasses stay recognizable as the framing changes.
video.example.machine-horizon.title: Machine Horizon
video.example.machine-horizon.descriptio: Armored machines clash across a desert plain. Watch the cuts from wide, dusty silhouettes to close shots of the moving armor.

video.prompts.drafts: These are starting prompts. Test them with your own inputs and adjust the motion or framing.
video.prompt.orbit.title: Perfume Orbit
video.prompt.orbit.text: Slowly orbit the perfume bottle clockwise on wet black stone. Keep the glass silhouette and packaging fixed while warm gold light moves across the edges. A thin layer of mist drifts behind the bottle. Finish on a centered hero frame. Sound: a low studio hum and two faint water droplets.
video.prompt.dolly.title: Slow Push-In
video.prompt.dolly.text: Begin with the full product in frame, then dolly straight toward its most textured detail. Keep the proportions, text, and logo fixed. Use shallow depth of field at the end and a soft room tone throughout. No cuts.
video.prompt.coffee.title: Coffee Steam
video.prompt.coffee.text: A locked close shot of a handmade ceramic cup on a walnut tray. Fresh coffee steams into a beam of morning light. A hand slides the saucer a few centimeters and leaves frame. Sound: the ceramic scrape, quiet birds, and the soft hiss of steam.
video.prompt.tabletop.title: Tabletop Reveal
video.prompt.tabletop.text: Start from the uploaded product photo. Ease the camera sideways from soft shadow into a window reflection. Keep the packaging edges, color, and logo stable. Finish with the product centered against the tabletop. Sound: gentle interior room tone.
video.prompt.water.title: Water and Glass
video.prompt.water.text: Hold the bottle still while a single bead of water runs down its front. Rack focus from the moving bead to the glass rim. Preserve the silhouette and lettering. Sound: one crisp water drop followed by silence.
video.prompt.dialogue.title: Two-Line Dialogue
video.prompt.dialogue.text: At a quiet dock at dawn, frame two friends in a medium two-shot. The person on the left says, "We missed the ferry." After a beat the person on the right replies, "Then we wait." Sound: soft water laps and clear dialogue, with no music.
video.prompt.forest.title: Forest Walk
video.prompt.forest.text: A hiker in a yellow rain jacket steps off a wooden bridge into a misty fir forest. Track slowly from behind at walking speed. Keep the rain jacket and backpack consistent. Sound: light rainfall, wet footsteps, and distant birds.
video.prompt.night.title: Rainy Street Tracking
video.prompt.night.text: A continuous low tracking shot follows a red bicycle along a rain-wet street at night. Reflections slide across the pavement. Keep a steady distance from the rear wheel. Sound: rolling tires, soft rain, and a single bell.
video.prompt.paper.title: Paper Landscape
video.prompt.paper.text: A folded paper boat glides through a layered cut-paper river. Track with the boat as the shore changes from blue hills to warm orange trees. Keep the paper edges crisp. Sound: gentle folded paper and a quiet stream.
video.prompt.stopmotion.title: Clay Sprout
video.prompt.stopmotion.text: In a locked close shot, a clay seed sprouts into a tiny three-leaf plant. Keep the stage, pot, and lighting fixed. Add slight stop-motion texture to the leaves. Sound: soft rustling and one wooden tap at the end.

video.faq.home.title: MAGI-2 FAQ
video.faq.home.model.q: What kind of model is MAGI-2?
video.faq.home.model.a: MAGI-2 is a video generation model that can create moving images and synchronized sound from prompts and media references. The MAGI-2 preview shows how dialogue, camera motion, and character performance can work together in one scene.
video.faq.home.publisher.a: Sand.ai developed and announced MAGI-2. Higgsfield publishes its own MAGI-2 examples and offers hosted access to the model.
video.faq.home.official.q: Where can I watch the official MAGI-2 preview?
video.faq.home.official.a: Open Sand.ai’s research preview in Sources below to see the original release. The MAGI-2 examples library also collects clips from the Sand.ai and Higgsfield showcases.
video.faq.home.generator.q: How do I generate a new clip in this studio?
video.faq.home.generator.a: Enter a text prompt or upload a starting image, then choose whether to include sound. The studio renders a 10-second video at 1080p.
video.faq.text.title: Text-to-video FAQ
video.faq.text.image.q: Can I add a photo to a text prompt?
video.faq.text.image.a: A text render starts with your prompt alone. To supply the first frame yourself, switch to Image to video and upload one JPG, PNG, or WebP under 10 MB.
video.faq.text.format.q: Which sizes and lengths work with text to video?
video.faq.text.format.a: Render a 10-second 1080p MP4. Choose 16:9, 9:16, 21:9, 4:3, 3:4, or 1:1 to frame your shot.
video.faq.text.credits.q: How are credits calculated for a text render?
video.faq.text.credits.a: The studio shows the credit cost before you generate. It reserves that amount on submission and restores it if the provider reports the job failed or was canceled.
video.faq.text.retention.q: How long can I retrieve a clip made from text?
video.faq.text.retention.a: My videos keeps the job in your history. The hosted MP4 may expire at the provider, so save a local copy when the render is ready.
video.faq.image.title: Image-to-video FAQ
video.faq.image.image.q: What makes a good starting image?
video.faq.image.image.a: Upload a sharp JPG, PNG, or WebP up to 10 MB as the first frame. You can also upload a last frame to guide where the shot ends.
video.faq.image.format.q: Does my starting image set the video format?
video.faq.image.format.a: The studio animates your still for 10 seconds. The 1080p MP4 follows your starting image’s aspect ratio.
video.faq.image.credits.q: What happens to my credits if an image render fails?
video.faq.image.credits.a: An image render uses the credits shown when you submit the job. If it fails or is canceled, those credits return to your balance.
video.faq.image.retention.q: Will the finished animation stay available online?
video.faq.image.retention.a: You can reopen the animation through My videos while its hosted file is available. Download the finished MP4 for long-term storage because the provider controls when hosted files expire.

video.guide.study.title: How to break down a MAGI-2 example
video.guide.study.intro: Start with one MAGI-2 example and watch it at full speed. Replay it with these three checks, then turn your notes into a brief for your next shot.
video.guide.study.frame: Pause on the first frame. Write down the shot size, where the subject sits, and which background lines lead toward it. Those details define the composition before anything moves.
video.guide.study.motion: Mark the moment the camera first moves. In Storm Wings, watch the fighter’s position against the background as the angle changes. Note whether the camera moves before, during, or after the action you want to emphasize.
video.guide.study.adapt: Replace the subject with your own while keeping the starting framing and the moment the move begins. Test that version as a short draft. Change the speed or angle only after reviewing the first result.
video.guide.product.title: Animate a product photo
video.guide.product.intro: Use one clean image and one camera move for the first pass.
video.guide.product.step1: Upload a sharp photo with visible product edges and space around the packaging. The 10-second video follows the orientation of your photo.
video.guide.product.step2: Ask for a slow orbit or push-in. Specify the label and package must keep their position, shape, and color. Check the first and last frames for lettering changes.
video.guide.product.step3: If the product drifts, simplify the movement or shorten the prompt. Save the best clip and record the prompt and aspect ratio.
video.guide.camera.title: Describe a camera move
video.guide.camera.intro: Write the beginning, one movement, and the ending in that order.
video.guide.camera.step1: Start with the framing. A wide shot shows the environment, a medium shot covers a person or full product, and a close-up shows texture or detail.
video.guide.camera.step2: Use an action you can picture, such as “dolly forward slowly” or “orbit clockwise”. Add a final framing instruction so the model has somewhere to end.
video.guide.camera.step3: If the clip feels hurried, remove competing moves. Change one instruction at a time so you can compare each result.
video.guide.sound.title: Write sound and dialogue
video.guide.sound.intro: Describe what the viewer hears and when it happens.
video.guide.sound.step1: Turn on Sound. Add one environmental sound that matches the shot, such as rain, footsteps, or a faint air conditioner.
video.guide.sound.step2: For dialogue, name who speaks and use short lines. Add a pause between speakers to give them time to finish.
video.guide.sound.step3: Play the clip with sound on. Check timing and word clarity. If music distracts from the dialogue, ask for room tone only.

video.article.title: How to study MAGI-2 video examples
video.article.lead: Pick a detail from a MAGI-2 clip that you want to try in your own shot. The guide shows how to describe a camera move, frame a product photo, or time dialogue.
video.article.overview.title: What is MAGI-2?
video.article.overview.p1: The Sand.ai MAGI-2 launch reel shows how a camera can follow a subject through a scene while the sound changes with the action. Compare a close-up with a wide shot before you decide what your first frame needs to show.
video.article.overview.p2: Try a similar technique in the MAGI-2 video generator. Start with a text prompt or an image to create a 10-second 1080p clip.
video.article.text.title: Turn a MAGI-2 reference into a text prompt
video.article.text.p1: A MAGI-2 prompt gives the scene a clear order. In a MAGI 2 AI demo, a visual effect can hide a cut. Replay the moment the movement changes, then write down the first frame, one action, and where your camera should end.
video.article.text.p2: For a ten-second coffee shot, try “hold on a cup in morning light while a hand turns the handle, then end on the rising steam.” Revise one camera instruction at a time so you can compare drafts.
video.article.image.title: Animate a product photo
video.article.image.p1: If you try the MAGI-2 video generator with a product reference, leave room around the edges for the camera to orbit. In this studio, upload a JPG, PNG, or WebP under 10 MB as your first frame.
video.article.image.p2: For a perfume shot, ask for a clockwise camera move as haze passes behind the glass. Compare the bottle shape and label in the first, middle, and last frames. Try a gentler move if the lettering drifts.
video.article.audio.title: Time dialogue and ambient sound
video.article.audio.p1: Listen to a MAGI-2 dialogue clip and notice the pauses between speakers. In your own prompt, name each speaker and keep the lines short enough to fit the clip. Turn on Sound to generate audio with the picture.
video.article.audio.p2: In the MAGI-2 preview, listen for a sound that lands on a visible action. Try timing a cup touching a saucer the same way. Switch Sound off for a silent loop.
video.article.audio.link: Read the sound and dialogue guide
video.article.format.title: Frame a landscape or portrait clip
video.article.format.p1: Choose 16:9 for wide camera moves or 9:16 for phone-first clips. Image-to-video renders follow the orientation of the starting image. In the reference clip, watch how the product stays near the center of the vertical frame.
video.article.format.p2: Check the framing and movement across the ten seconds. For your next render, keep the frame size and adjust one camera instruction.
video.article.review.title: Compare the render and download the MP4
video.article.review.p1: When comparing MAGI 2 AI footage with your own render, match the opening framing before you judge the camera move. Check whether the subject stays recognizable and the last frame reads clearly. Play it again with audio to check timing.
video.article.review.p2: Check render progress in My videos and download the finished MP4 to keep a copy. Save the prompt and settings if you plan to make another shot in the same style.
video.insight.text.title: Write a prompt the camera can follow
video.insight.text.p1: Describe what the first frame shows, how the subject moves, and where you want to finish. For a street scene, choose whether the camera follows a bicycle or holds on the bike passing through the frame. Those choices create different shots even when the same objects appear.
video.insight.text.p2: A short soundtrack note can specify rain on pavement, rolling tires, and a distant bell. Keep dialogue brief enough to finish within ten seconds. If a draft moves too quickly, simplify the action and generate another version with the same frame size.
video.insight.image.title: Keep the details of the original photo
video.insight.image.p1: Choose a starting image with clean edges around the subject. A gentle push-in or shallow orbit is a useful first test for product packaging. Use your prompt to name the details you care about, such as the cap height, glass color, and front label.
video.insight.image.p2: Compare the first and last frames with your reference. If the logo changes as the camera moves, use a steadier camera instruction on the next render. Check the sides of the image when preparing a vertical version.
video.insight.examples.title: How to study a MAGI-2 example
video.insight.examples.p1: Watch one clip for framing and again for sound. In the shot-cut example, observe how movement carries across a cut. In the dialogue example, compare the shot scale before and after a response. The same editing choices can help you describe a short scene of your own.
video.insight.examples.p2: Each clip links to its showcase at Sand.ai or Higgsfield. Where an example has documented inputs, they appear alongside the video. When you try a related prompt in the studio, use it to explore a technique you saw.
video.insight.prompts.title: Adapt a template to your own shot
video.insight.prompts.p1: Replace the example subject with your own, then choose which motion the viewer should notice. Save one version of the prompt before changing anything. When comparing results, try just one change to the camera, lighting, or timing so you can tell what changed the shot.
video.insight.prompts.p2: An image template assumes that you already have a clear starting frame. A text template describes that frame before it asks the camera to move. Choose the template that matches the material you are starting with.
video.insight.pricing.title: Plan credits for drafts and final clips
video.insight.pricing.p1: Pick a pack based on how many clips you want to create. A one-video pack is available on your first purchase. Unused credits from one-time packs stay in your balance.
video.insight.pricing.p2: Every submission shows its own charge. A failed or canceled job returns its credits. A completed draft and a new variation are separate renders, so budget for another submission when testing different camera moves.
